subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Nonmetal samples
hotspots.description: A set of nonmetal samples: a matte lump of sulfur, a dark block of carbon, and a small cloud of oxygen gas. All dull, none shiny.
hotspots.positionHint: The cluster of samples at the center of the scene.
hotspots.function: Shows real nonmetal samples with their dull, matte look.

hotspots.label: Brittleness
hotspots.description: When struck, this sulfur lump shatters into fragments rather than bending like a metal — brittle is the nonmetal way to break.
hotspots.positionHint: The sulfur lump on the right, where the mallet lands when the brittle-test layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows that nonmetal solids shatter instead of bending.

hotspots.label: Gas state
hotspots.description: The drifting cloud is oxygen gas — many nonmetals exist as gases at room temperature.
hotspots.positionHint: The small soft cloud above the samples, drifting when the gas-state layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows that many nonmetals are gases at room temperature.

hotspots.label: Nonmetal region
hotspots.description: The highlighted zone on the periodic table is where nonmetals live — the upper right, a smaller family than the metals.
hotspots.positionHint: The highlighted zone in the upper-right corner of the table section below the samples.
hotspots.function: Shows where nonmetals sit on the periodic table.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. The nonmetal samples float centered above a table section, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Color on the mesh is restrained: the sulfur lump is a soft muted mustard, the carbon block a matte graphite, the oxygen cloud a barely-there translucent pale blue-grey. Strong saturated color is reserved entirely for the small flat hotspot dots (molecular green / amber / slate / coral accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Sulfur lump: matte muted mustard, roughness ~0.7. Carbon block: matte graphite, roughness ~0.6. Oxygen cloud: translucent pale blue-grey, alpha ~0.25, roughness ~0.5. Table tiles: paper-white, roughness ~0.55. No emissive channels anywhere — any highlight or animation is handled by app runtime UI, not baked into the asset.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a set of nonmetal samples with their behavior, built to be read as 'the dull, brittle, gas-prone opposites of the metals.' Four procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a small cluster of samples at the center — (a) a lumpy matte mustard sulfur chunk (~0.8 across, softened blob), (b) a dark matte graphite block (~0.7 cube, chamfered), and (c) a soft translucent pale-blue-grey cloud (several overlapping flattened spheres, alpha ~0.25) representing oxygen gas, hovering above. No shine anywhere.

2) BRITTLE TEST (toggleable layer): a small matte-graphite mallet swings down onto the sulfur lump (the app animates the strike); the lump briefly splits into 3-4 fragments that separate gently. Sulfur, mallet, and fragments all matte.

3) TABLE REGION (toggleable layer): below the samples, a flat section of periodic table (paper-white tiles, ~9 x 5). The upper-right cluster of tiles (last 3 columns, top 2 rows) gets a faint muted cool cast and slight raise — the nonmetal region, separated from the metal region by a thin stair-step boundary line.

4) GAS STATE (toggleable layer): the oxygen cloud expands slightly and drifts in a slow gentle loop (the app animates the drift).

Camera: framed so the sample cluster is large and centered with the table slab below; auto-rotate default. Budget 8-12k triangles. Named nodes: SulfurLump, GraphiteBlock, OxygenCloud, Mallet, Fragments_01-04, TableSlab, NonmetalRegion, StepBoundary. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer; no text on the mesh.
